title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 30
paragraphs: So the Thessalians proposed. For the Phokians alone of all the peoples in those parts were not siding with the Medes — for no other reason, I suppose, than their enmity with the Thessalians; and had the Thessalians supported the Greek cause, I believe the Phokians would have been on the side of the Medes. When the Thessalians put this to them, the Phokians said they would not give the money, and that they had just as much freedom to take the Median side as the Thessalians, if they wanted to for other reasons; but they would not willingly be traitors to Greece.
